title: Rule node-graph editor (SCR-082) with lossless IR round-trip
body:
## Context
Owner decision #11 (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Product, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md`) requires **two** rule authoring surfaces in v1 — a structured form/condition-list editor (E36) and a visual node-graph editor (this epic) — that compile to **one** rule IR executed by **one** runtime (E35). This epic delivers the node-graph surface: screen **SCR-082** (`/rules/:ruleId/graph`) and components **CMP-146..CMP-153**, **CMP-234..CMP-238**, covering **US-RULE-005** (node-graph editor) and the graph half of **US-RULE-006** (editor round-trip switching), plus the graph rendering of the metric/action vocabulary (**US-RULE-002**, **US-RULE-003**).

Two properties make this epic hard and make it release-blocking rather than cosmetic:
1. **Lossless round-trip.** `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4 defines the canonical IR (sorted keys, `node_id`s renumbered in DFS order, `graph_layout` dropped) and its sha256. Form→IR→graph→IR→form must leave that hash unchanged; where a graph exceeds the *form subset* the UI must say so explicitly (`Unsupported in form view`) rather than silently mangling the rule.
2. **Accessibility.** `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146 calls the graph canvas *the second-highest a11y risk after the chart engine*. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` and the R3 quality gate require that **every** graph operation is also reachable from a keyboard node-list panel (`Alt+L`) / command palette, and that the form editor is an always-available equal-status alternative.

The roadmap places E37 in **S17–S18** of the R3 train, after E35 (IR, compiler, runtime) and E36 (form editor) per the dependency graph in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screen:** SCR-082 Rule editor — node-graph mode (`/rules/:ruleId/graph`), including the palette, canvas, node inspector drawer, validation panel, minimap, round-trip indicator and the `Alt+L` keyboard node-list panel.
- **Components:** CMP-146 NodeGraphCanvas, CMP-147 TriggerNode, CMP-148 ConditionNode, CMP-149 ActionNode, CMP-150 LogicGateNode, CMP-151 CommentNode, CMP-152 NodeGraphEdge, CMP-153 NodeInspectorDrawer, CMP-236 NodePalette, CMP-237 NodePort, CMP-238 Minimap; reuse of CMP-157 MetricPickerCombobox, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-234 ValidationPanel, CMP-235 EditorModeToggle.
- **Frontend package:** `packages/rule-graph` — pure graph⇄IR adapter (`toGraph(ir)`, `toIr(graph)`), typed port model, cycle/orphan analysis, canonicalisation client-side mirror, auto-layout.
- **User stories:** US-RULE-005 (Must, primary), US-RULE-006 (Must, graph side), US-RULE-002 and US-RULE-003 (Must, graph rendering of the vocabularies), US-RULE-001 (Must, round-trip/canonical-hash consumption), US-RULE-007/US-RULE-008/US-RULE-010/US-RULE-011 surfaces consumed (scope chip, simulate/arm entry points, error and conflict display) — authored in E35/E36, re-used here.
- **API consumed (no new endpoints):** `GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary`, `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile`, `POST /api/v1/rules/validate`, `GET/PUT /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}`, `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/versions`, `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/simulate`, `PUT /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/mode`.
- **WS consumed:** topic `rules` (`RuleUpdate`, §15.6) for armed-state/engine-availability banners.
- **DB touched (read/write via API only):** `rules.editor`, `rule_versions.ir` / `ir_hash` (the `graph_layout` presentation block lives inside the version document and is excluded from the hash).
- **Feature flag:** `rules.node_editor` / `rules.graph_editor` (default on in dev, off in prod until design-QA and a11y gates pass).
- Design tickets D01–D06, QA tickets Q01–Q06, security tickets X01–X02, docs/ADR task T03.

## Out of scope
- The rule IR, compiler, runtime, evaluation semantics, simulation backend and rule versioning — **E35**.
- The form/condition-list editor itself, templates gallery (SCR-083) and the form-side round-trip indicator — **E36**.
- Rules list (SCR-080), simulation panel (SCR-084), arming dialog (SCR-085), IR inspector (SCR-088) — owned by E35/E36; E37 only links to them.
- Alerts authoring re-using the IR — **E40**. Risk caps/kill-switch — **E39**.
- Any collaborative/multi-user live co-editing of a graph. Any new metric or action beyond the published vocabulary. Android (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A rule can be authored end-to-end on the canvas
  Given a draft rule and the node palette
  When I add a trigger, a condition, a logic gate and an action node and connect them
  Then the graph validates continuously, "errors: 0" is shown, and saving stores a rule version whose IR compiles from the graph model via POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile

Scenario: Round-trip is lossless on a 30-rule corpus
  Given the round-trip corpus of >=30 rules authored in the form editor (E36)
  When each is opened in the node editor and saved without edit
  Then the canonical IR hash is unchanged for every rule, and the same holds in the reverse direction

Scenario: A graph outside the form subset is declared, not mangled
  Given a graph using nested arithmetic or a fan-out edge feeding two actions
  Then the header shows "Unsupported in form view", the offending nodes are badged on canvas and listed in the Alt+L node list, and switching to the form editor renders those parts read-only while preserving them byte-for-byte on save

Scenario: Keyboard-only authoring (a11y, failure of the canvas path)
  Given a user who never uses a pointer
  When they add, connect, inspect, rename and delete nodes via the palette, Alt+L node list and node/port keyboard-connect flow
  Then every operation available by mouse completes, is announced in a live region, and shares one undo/redo stack

Scenario: Invalid connection and cycle (error)
  When a boolean output is connected to a numeric input, or a node output is connected back into its own upstream
  Then the connection is refused with an inline typed explanation, the cycle path is highlighted and enumerated in the node list, and the IR never contains the invalid edge

Scenario: Performance at scale
  Given a 200-node graph
  Then pan/zoom sustains 60 fps on reference hardware and the compile+diff round-trip check completes within 500 ms p95 for a 100-node graph
```

## Technical notes / design
- Library: React Flow (DOM-rendered nodes — chosen precisely because nodes are real focusable DOM elements, per CMP-146 and the spike E37-K01). Nodes/edges are controlled state owned by `packages/rule-graph`, not by the library.
- Adapter contract (`packages/rule-graph`): `toGraph(ir: RuleIr): GraphModel` (auto-layout when `graph_layout` is absent) and `toIr(graph: GraphModel): RuleIrDraft`; both pure and property-tested. Server `POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile` remains the single source of truth for the canonical IR and `ir_hash`; the client adapter never asserts its own hash as authoritative.
- Port typing: `boolean | number | price | side | action | trigger`; the compatibility matrix lives in one table consumed by both the connect handler and the keyboard-connect flow so pointer and keyboard reject identically.
- Presentation split: node x/y, collapsed state and comment nodes live in `graph_layout` and are excluded from the canonical hash (`24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4 guarantee 3) — moving a box must never create a rule version.
- Validation: diagnostics come from `POST /rules/validate` on the compiled IR and are rendered through the shared CMP-234 ValidationPanel with `anchor.kind = "node"|"edge"`, guaranteeing the form and graph editors report *identical* diagnostics.
- Safety: CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice is non-dismissible in this editor; arming is never performed here — the editor links to SCR-085.

## Test plan
Unit (adapter, port matrix, cycle/orphan analysis, auto-layout stability), property/fuzz (round-trip over generated IR documents, >=10 000 per CI run per US-RULE-001 NFR), contract (vocabulary + compile + validate response shapes), integration (compile against a live backend), E2E Playwright (author, connect, validate, switch editors, save, simulate entry), a11y (axe + keyboard-only authoring suite, a named CI gate), performance (200-node fps benchmark, compile+diff p95). Coverage: >=80% frontend, >=85% for `packages/rule-graph`.

## Security notes
The node editor authors documents that, once armed, can place and cancel orders. Threats (STRIDE, `04-security-program.md`): tampering (a client-side-built graph that compiles to a different IR than displayed), elevation of privilege (authoring actions scoped to accounts the user cannot trade), repudiation (a graph edit that changes what an armed rule does without an audit trail), DoS (a pathological graph that stalls the compiler). Controls: server-side compile and validation are authoritative; RBAC `rules:write` with `granted_accounts` scoping; every save emits `rule.graph_saved` / `rule.roundtrip_verified`; node/edge caps enforced server-side; editing an armed rule requires the disarm-or-new-draft path (US-RULE-006). Data classification: financial-control configuration (not PII, not secret) — but integrity-critical.

## Accessibility notes
Mandatory: keyboard node-list panel (`Alt+L`) as an equal-status authoring path, roving-tabindex node navigation, focusable typed ports with spoken direction/type/connection state, `Enter`-based keyboard connect, edge delete from the keyboard, focus-to-anchor from every diagnostic, reduced-motion variant (no edge animation), and the always-available "Switch to form view" toggle. The minimap is `aria-hidden` and must never be the only route to anything. WCAG 2.2 AA; axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass recorded.

## Performance notes
200 nodes at 60 fps (SCR-082 §Performance); edge routing memoised; inspector edits must not re-layout the graph; compile+diff round-trip check <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node graph and runs on save and mode switch only, never per keystroke; the editor bundle is lazily code-split so it does not count against budget #9 (initial bundle).

## Observability
Frontend telemetry and backend audit: `rule.graph_saved`, `rule.roundtrip_verified {result}`, `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved {choice}` (audited), plus non-audited analytics `rule.graph_node_added {type}`, `rule.graph_autolayout_used`, `rule.graph_keyboard_authoring_used`. Metrics: `rule_graph_compile_duration_ms` histogram, `rule_graph_roundtrip_mismatch_total` counter (alert on any non-zero in staging), `rule_graph_node_count` histogram.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Exit criterion 5 of R3 proven: a corpus of >=30 rules round-trips form↔graph with identical canonical IR hashes (E37-Q03).
- [ ] a11y gate green: axe clean, keyboard-only authoring suite green, manual screen-reader pass recorded (E37-Q05).
- [ ] perf gate green: 200-node 60 fps, compile+diff <=500 ms p95 (E37-Q04).
- [ ] STRIDE model finalised and findings closed; security sign-off (E37-X01, E37-X02).
- [ ] Coverage >=80% frontend / >=85% `packages/rule-graph`; zero open P0/P1.
- [ ] Docs updated: `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-082, `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146..153/234..238, `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4 if behaviour diverged, ADR-0007 addendum (E37-T03).
- [ ] Storybook stories for every CMP in scope, design-QA sign-off (E37-D06), QA sign-off (E37-Q06).
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at a Sprint Review against staging (demo).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded for `rules.node_editor` per environment.
- [ ] Design-ahead verified at sprint planning: E37-D05 Done in Sprint 15, >=2 sprints before E37-S01 (or a recorded Architect + CDO waiver).
- [ ] Delivery-engineering points re-checked against the roadmap 26 pts at epic close; variance >15% raised with the Product and Architecture owners.

## Estimate reconciliation (roadmap 26 pts vs. epic rollup 65 pts)
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 records **26 points** for E37. That is the roadmap's **delivery-engineering** estimate — the Story and build-Task work that builds the node editor. This backlog file additionally itemises design, spike, QA and security work that the roadmap carries inside its train-level design/QA/security allowances, so the epic rollup (sum of children, per the schema rule "epics: sum of children") is larger. The two numbers reconcile as:

Confirmed deliberate, not drift. The earlier 27-pt reading counted E37-T03, the docs/ADR reconciliation, which is now correctly classified as a `Chore` alongside its E36-T02 precedent; delivery engineering is **26 pts, 0% variance** against the roadmap. The 65-pt rollup sits **at** the 65-point hard cap for a single epic, so **E37 has no headroom**: any new child must be paid for by descoping **E37-T02** (auto-layout, node search, minimap — already the named R5 descoping candidate in `30-release-roadmap.md` §12) rather than by growing the epic. Re-check at epic close and raise any variance >15% with the Product and Architecture owners.

## Design-ahead compliance

Consuming stories start in **Sprint 17** (S01, S02, S03) and **Sprint 18** (S04, S05) — a **2-sprint** (respectively 3-sprint) design-ahead buffer, satisfying `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 with **no waiver required**. ## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. **Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. title: UX research: how rule authors reason about a node graph vs a condition list
body:
## Context
E37 introduces SCR-082, the product's only free-form 2D authoring canvas. It is a genuinely new interaction for this product: every other authoring surface (order ticket, profiles, the E36 form editor) is a linear form. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-RULE-005 asserts the graph exists so "complex logic is easier to see", but we have no evidence about *which* logic the owner and the manager persona actually find hard to read in the form, nor about how they expect a graph to behave (dataflow-like, or a visual syntax for one boolean tree + action list, which is what ADR-0007 actually delivers).

Getting this wrong is expensive twice over: the canvas is the most costly surface to build, and per `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146 it is the second-highest accessibility risk in the product. The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence) requires this research to conclude before D02 draws anything, and at least two sprints ahead of the Sprint 17 frontend work. This ticket therefore runs in **Sprint 13**, in parallel with E36-D01 (form-editor research) so the same participants can be asked about both authoring surfaces in one session series, and so the whole E37 design chain can finish by the end of Sprint 15.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Semi-structured sessions (45 min, >=3 participants across the P1 Owner and P2 Manager personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, including at least one participant who prefers keyboard-first operation) covering: which real rules they want, how they currently express "A AND (B OR C)", what they expect a node to *be*, and what they expect `auto-layout` to do to their hand-placed boxes.
- A concept test using the SCR-082 ASCII wireframe in `14-screens-catalogue.md` plus one alternative framing (palette-left canvas vs. an outline-plus-canvas split) — measure whether participants can read the pictured "ATR trail 2x" rule aloud correctly.
- A comprehension test of the four round-trip indicator states defined for SCR-082 (`Round-trips ✓`, `Unsupported in form view`, `Round-trip mismatch`, `Not verified`): do participants understand what they lose by switching editors, and what "unsupported in form view" means for their rule?
- A decision test on the vocabulary used on canvas: node/port/edge vs. block/socket/wire vs. step/input/link — the chosen words must then be used identically in UI copy, `aria-label`s, validation messages and docs.
- Findings deck + a one-page "design principles for the node editor" note that D02/D03/D04 are held against, plus any resulting update to `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md` F10 and `docs/plan/10-personas.md`.
- Explicit written answers to five questions: (1) is the graph a *reading* aid or an *authoring* aid for this user? (2) is the form editor the expected default entry point, with the graph opened for inspection? (3) how should the four round-trip states be worded? (4) what is the node vocabulary? (5) does auto-layout need an explicit undo affordance beyond `Ctrl+Z`?

## Out of scope
- Any hi-fi visual work (→ E37-D02), motion specs (→ E37-D03), a11y design review (→ E37-D04).
- Usability testing of built software (→ E37-Q06 exploratory charter).
- Research on the form editor (owned by E36's design work).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All five questions answered with evidence
  Given at least three completed sessions across the Owner and Manager personas
  When findings are written up
  Then each of the five questions has a written answer citing specific participant evidence, not designer preference

Scenario: The round-trip states are comprehensible
  Given participants are shown the four round-trip indicator states in isolation
  When asked what each means for their rule
  Then either >=2 of 3 participants explain each state correctly, or the failing state's wording is rewritten and re-tested within this ticket

Scenario: A keyboard-first participant is included (edge)
```

title: Design-system tokens and motion spec for node, port, edge and canvas primitives
body:
## Context
The node editor introduces primitives the design system does not yet own: a node container with typed ports, an edge, a connect-in-progress state, a minimap and a canvas surface. `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` already reserves the component IDs (CMP-146..153, CMP-236..238) and names tokens (`color.node.*`, `color.edge.default/selected`, `color.port.*`, `color.surface.canvas`, `color.surface.sunken`), but the token values, the motion behaviour and the Storybook contract do not exist. Without this ticket each node type would be styled ad hoc, which `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 explicitly forbids ("any new component has a design-system entry, not an ad hoc one-off").

Motion matters here specifically because edges animate on connect and auto-layout moves every node at once — both are exactly the kinds of motion that trigger vestibular issues and both must have a reduced-motion path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Token definitions (light + dark themes, both density modes) for `color.node.trigger|condition|action|logic|comment`, `color.node.border.{default,selected,error,warning}`, `color.port.{in,out,connected,compatible,incompatible}`, `color.edge.{default,selected,invalid}`, `color.surface.canvas`, `radius.node`, `space.node.*` — each contrast-verified against its background in both themes.
- Motion spec: connect-in-progress edge preview, connection-made confirmation, node add/remove, selection change, auto-layout transition (duration, easing, stagger, maximum total duration), minimap viewport tracking, inspector drawer open/close (inherits CMP-046). Each with an explicit `prefers-reduced-motion` variant that removes movement rather than merely shortening it.
- Design-system entries for CMP-146, CMP-147..CMP-152, CMP-153, CMP-236, CMP-237, CMP-238: props table alignment with the catalogue API sketches, the Storybook story list named in the catalogue (e.g. CMP-146: EmptyCanvas, SimpleChain, BranchingLogic, ReadOnly, KeyboardNavDemo, FormViewToggleDemo), and usage/anti-usage guidance.
- Focus-ring specification for canvas-adjacent focusables (nodes, ports, edges) reusing CMP-035's shared focus-ring utility so the ring is visually identical to the rest of the product.
- Density/zoom tiers: what node chrome is shown at each zoom tier, specified as discrete tiers so rendering can switch cheaply.

## Out of scope
- Hi-fi screen composition (E37-D02); the a11y review itself (E37-D04); implementation of any token or story (E37-S01/S02).
- Chart-engine canvas tokens — separate, owned by the charting epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every new token is contrast-verified in both themes
  Given the token set for nodes, ports and edges
  When contrast is measured against every surface they appear on, in light and dark
  Then text meets 4.5:1 and graphical boundaries meet 3:1, with the measurements recorded in the token documentation

Scenario: Reduced motion removes movement
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  Then auto-layout repositions nodes with no animated transit, edge previews do not animate, and the spec states this explicitly per animation rather than as a blanket note

Scenario: Auto-layout motion has a hard ceiling
  Given a 200-node graph is auto-laid-out
  Then the specified transition completes within 400 ms total regardless of node count, with stagger capped rather than per-node accumulating

Scenario: A node type has no distinguishable non-colour treatment (failure)
  Given two node types are distinguished only by hue in a draft
  Then the spec is corrected to add a shape, icon or label difference before sign-off, because status and type must never be colour-only
```

## Technical notes / design
Tokens follow the naming and theming conventions in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; emitted as design tokens consumed by the web app's theme layer, not hand-copied hex. Motion values expressed as tokens (`motion.duration.*`, `motion.easing.*`) so reduced-motion overrides happen at the token layer. The zoom tiers are specified as a table (zoom range → visible chrome) that E37-S01 implements verbatim.

## Test plan
Storybook visual-regression baselines exist for each new component's story list (implemented in E37-S01/S02, specified here); contrast checks recorded in the token docs; reduced-motion variants captured as separate visual-regression stories.

## Security notes
N/A — presentation tokens only. (One exception: the "node-only"/unsupported and error treatments are safety-relevant communication, so they may not be de-emphasised for aesthetic reasons; this is stated in the usage guidance.)

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is where the non-colour encoding rule is made structural: every node type, port state and diagnostic severity has a glyph or shape in addition to hue. Focus rings must be visible against the canvas surface in both themes. Reduced-motion variants are mandatory, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
Zoom tiers are specified so the renderer can drop text and detail at low zoom; motion is capped so auto-layout on a 200-node graph cannot blow the frame budget.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Tokens defined, contrast-verified, published to the design-token source of record.
- [ ] Motion spec complete with a reduced-motion variant per animation.
- [ ] Design-system entries written for CMP-146..153, CMP-236..238, aligned with `15-component-catalogue.md` props and story lists.

## Scope / Deliverables

The keyboard authoring map becomes the direct source of the E37-Q05 audit script and the keyboard-only interaction tests in E37-S05 — one row of the map per test case. That traceability is itself checked at sign-off.

N/A — but note that arming (a security-relevant action) is deliberately *not* reachable from the canvas; the review confirms the editor's keyboard map contains no arm shortcut, so step-up auth via SCR-085 cannot be bypassed by a hotkey.

This ticket *is* the accessibility work product: WCAG 2.2 AA mapped criterion by criterion for a canvas-adjacent surface, with particular attention to 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.5.8 Target Size, 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value and 4.1.3 Status Messages.

The live-region announcement strategy must be specified to coalesce (one announcement per completed operation, not per intermediate state) so screen-reader users are not flooded during rapid edits.

Specifies the `rule.graph_keyboard_authoring_used` analytics event so adoption of the keyboard path is measurable rather than assumed.

## Scope / Deliverables

1. Does React Flow (current major version, pinned) sustain **60 fps pan/zoom on a 200-node / ~260-edge graph** on the reference hardware in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1, inside Electron and Chromium, with our node chrome (not stock demo nodes)?
2. Can nodes, ports and edges each be made individually focusable with roving tabindex, without fighting the library's own pointer-first interaction layer, and can a **keyboard connect** (focus output port → `Enter` → arrow to target port → `Enter`) be implemented on top of the library's controlled state?

title: Build packages/rule-graph: graph<->IR adapter, typed ports, analysis
body:
## Context
Everything in E37 depends on one pure, well-tested translation layer between the canonical rule IR (`24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2/§11.3) and the editor's graph model. Putting that logic inside React components would make the round-trip property tests (US-RULE-001 NFR: >=10 000 generated documents per CI run) impossible to run cheaply and would couple the guarantee to the rendering library chosen in E37-K01.

`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` C10 already names the backend counterparts `RuleCompiler` and `RuleDecompiler` (`to_form(ir)`, `to_graph(ir)`). The backend remains authoritative: `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile` returns the canonical IR and `ir_hash`. This package is the *client-side mirror* used for instant feedback, layout ownership and analysis — it must never claim authority over the hash.

## Scope / Deliverables
- New workspace package `packages/rule-graph` (TypeScript, no React dependency, no DOM dependency).
- `toGraph(ir: RuleIr, layout?: GraphLayout): GraphModel` — expands the IR condition DAG and action list into typed nodes (`trigger`, `condition`, `action`, `logicGate`, `comment` per CMP-146's `NodeGraphNode`) and edges, applying stored `graph_layout` when present and requesting auto-layout (E37-T02) when absent.
- `toIr(graph: GraphModel): { ir: RuleIrDraft; layout: GraphLayout }` — inverse, splitting semantics from presentation so `graph_layout` (node x/y, collapsed state, comment nodes) is carried separately and excluded from the canonical hash per `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4 guarantee 3.
- `canonicalise(ir): string` and `hash(ir): string` — a faithful client-side mirror of the server rule (sorted keys, normalised numbers, `node_id`s renumbered in DFS order, `graph_layout` dropped, sha256), used only for optimistic UI; a contract test asserts it agrees with `POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile` on the fixture corpus.
- Port type model and the **compatibility matrix** over `boolean | number | price | side | action | trigger`, exported as one table consumed by both pointer and keyboard connect paths, with a human-readable reason string per incompatible pair.
- Graph analysis: `findCycles(graph)` (returns the offending path, not just a boolean), `findOrphans(graph)` (nodes reaching no action), `findDanglingPorts(graph)` (required inputs unconnected), `isFormRepresentable(ir)` (the form subset test from `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4: trigger + two-level `all_of`/`any_of` boolean tree + flat action list + limits; nested arithmetic, `n_of`, multi-level nesting and fan-out edges are graph-only) returning the list of offending node ids and a plain-language reason each.
- Type generation from the published schema: types derive from `GET /api/v1/schemas/rule-ir.json` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §"served from the generated artefacts") at build time — never hand-written.

## Out of scope
- Any React component, canvas rendering or styling (E37-S01/S02).
- Auto-layout implementation (E37-T02 — this package exposes the hook point only).
- Server-side compile/validate (E35). Vocabulary fetching/caching UI (E37-S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Round-trip is hash-stable on the fixture corpus
  Given every rule in the shared fixture corpus
  When toGraph then toIr is applied
  Then canonicalise(result) equals canonicalise(original) for all of them, and the client hash equals the ir_hash returned by POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile

Scenario: Presentation never changes the hash
  Given a graph whose node positions, collapsed states and comment nodes are all modified
  When toIr is applied
  Then the canonical hash is unchanged and the layout differences appear only in the returned GraphLayout

Scenario: Form-subset detection is precise
  Given a rule with nested arithmetic, an n_of node, three-level boolean nesting or an output feeding two actions
  Then isFormRepresentable returns false and names each offending node id with a plain-language reason; given any rule inside the subset it returns true

Scenario: Cycle detection returns the path (error)
  Given a graph containing a cycle
  Then findCycles returns the ordered node path forming the cycle, and toIr refuses to emit an IR rather than emitting one containing the cycle

Scenario: Property fuzz (edge)
  Given 10000 randomly generated valid IR documents from the shared generator
  When each is passed through toGraph -> toIr
  Then the canonical hash is unchanged for every document, and any document that cannot be represented throws a named error rather than returning a lossy result
```

## Technical notes / design
```ts
export type PortType = "boolean" | "number" | "price" | "side" | "action" | "trigger";
export interface GraphNode { id: string; type: "trigger"|"condition"|"action"|"logicGate"|"comment";
  irNodeId?: string; data: Record<string, unknown>; }
export interface GraphEdge { id: string; source: string; sourcePort: string; target: string; targetPort: string; }
export interface GraphModel { nodes: GraphNode[]; edges: GraphEdge[]; }
export interface GraphLayout { positions: Record<string, {x:number;y:number}>; collapsed: string[]; comments: CommentNode[]; }
export const PORT_COMPAT: Record<PortType, { accepts: PortType[]; reason: (from: PortType) => string }>;
```
`irNodeId` preserves the IR's stable `node_id` so layout survives edits (`24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2/§3654 rationale: without stable node ids, form↔graph round-tripping is impossible). Canonicalisation follows JCS-style sorted keys and normalised numbers (`1.50` → `1.5`) per US-RULE-001. All functions are pure and synchronous; no fetch, no globals.

- Contract: client `hash()` vs server `POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile` `ir_hash` over the corpus, run against a live backend in CI integration stage.
- Coverage target: **>=85%** (engine-class package).

## Security notes
Tampering is the relevant STRIDE class: the client adapter must never be trusted to decide what gets stored. Saves send the editor model to the server, which compiles and validates authoritatively; the client hash is advisory only and this is asserted by a test that a server/client hash disagreement surfaces as the blocking `Round-trip mismatch` state rather than being auto-resolved client-side. The package performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Node and edge counts are bounded (matching the server's caps) so a pathological pasted document cannot hang the editor thread.

## Accessibility notes

## Performance notes

This story stands up SCR-082 (`/rules/:ruleId/graph`) as a working authoring surface: the canvas (CMP-146 NodeGraphCanvas), the categorised searchable palette (CMP-236 NodePalette), typed connection points (CMP-237 NodePort), edges (CMP-152 NodeGraphEdge) and the minimap mount (CMP-238). Design is handed over in E37-D05; the library and any node cap are settled by E37-K01; the IR translation lives in `packages/rule-graph` (E37-T01).

## Scope / Deliverables

- CMP-146 NodeGraphCanvas: controlled nodes/edges state owned by the app (not the library), pan (`Space+drag`, wheel), zoom (wheel, `Ctrl+0` reset), selection, multi-select, `Del` delete selection, `Ctrl+A` select all, marquee select; zoom/density tiers per the D03 tier table.
- CMP-236 NodePalette: categories (triggers, metrics, comparators, logic gates, actions, comments) built from `GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary`; search with no-results state; drag-to-canvas **and** select+`Enter` insertion (the non-drag path is mandatory per CMP-236's a11y contract and is implemented here, not deferred).
- CMP-237 NodePort: typed input/output ports rendered per node, each a focusable element with a name stating direction, type and connection state; pointer connect with live compatibility feedback using the `PORT_COMPAT` matrix from `packages/rule-graph`; incompatible drops refused with the matrix's inline reason string.
- CMP-152 NodeGraphEdge: bezier routing, default/selected/invalid-preview/labelled states, memoised routing, click-to-select, `Delete` to remove.
- Empty state ("Start from a trigger" hint), editing state, read-only state (armed rule viewed without editing), engine/vocabulary-unavailable banner.
- Undo/redo stack (`Ctrl+Z`/`Ctrl+Shift+Z`) covering add, delete, connect, disconnect, move — one stack shared with the keyboard path added in E37-S05.
- Dirty-state tracking and navigation guard (unsaved edits prompt to apply or discard, per US-RULE-006 "Unsaved changes").
- Save via `PUT /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}` with the compiled model from `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile`; optimistic-concurrency handling (reject with the version conflict error rather than last-writer-wins, per US-RULE-006).
- Storybook stories for CMP-146/152/236/237/238 exactly as listed in `15-component-catalogue.md`.

## Out of scope
- Node type bodies, inspector drawer and vocabulary parameter editing → **E37-S02**.
- Validation/diagnostics rendering → **E37-S03**. Round-trip indicator and editor switching → **E37-S04**. Keyboard authoring, node-list panel and live-region announcements → **E37-S05**. Auto-layout, node search-and-jump, minimap behaviour → **E37-T02**.
- Arming (SCR-085), simulation (SCR-084), rules list (SCR-080).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Author a minimal graph by pointer
  Given a draft rule opened at /rules/:ruleId/graph
  When I drag a trigger, a condition and an action node from the palette and connect them port to port
  Then edges render, the graph is held in app-owned state, and saving stores a version whose IR was compiled by POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile

Scenario: Incompatible connection is refused with a reason
  When I drag from a boolean output onto a numeric input
  Then the drop is refused, the target port shows the incompatible state, and the reason string from the port compatibility matrix is displayed inline

Scenario: Non-drag insertion works
  When I select a palette entry and press Enter
  Then the node is inserted, connected to the current selection where types allow, and becomes the new selection

Scenario: Viewer is denied (security edge)
  Given a user with the viewer role
  When they navigate directly to /rules/:ruleId/graph
  Then the route is not rendered, the API returns 403, no rule content is exposed, and an audit row is written

Scenario: Concurrent save is rejected (error)
  Given the same rule was saved from another tab after this editor loaded
  When I save
  Then an optimistic-concurrency error names the other editor and session and offers reload-and-reapply; no silent overwrite occurs

Scenario: Feature flag off
  Given rules.node_editor is disabled
  Then the graph route and the graph entry points in SCR-080/SCR-081 are absent, and the form editor remains fully usable
```

## Technical notes / design
State: `GraphModel` from `packages/rule-graph` is the single source of truth; the graph library receives derived props and emits intents which the reducer applies — no library-internal mutable state. Undo/redo is a command stack over that reducer so E37-S05's keyboard commands reuse it verbatim. Vocabulary is fetched once and cached (SCR-081 §Performance: "vocabulary cached"); a stale/unavailable vocabulary renders the palette disabled with the engine-unavailable banner rather than an empty palette. Compile is called on save and on mode switch only — never per keystroke or per drag (SCR-082 §Performance). Node/edge caps from E37-K01's ADR are enforced client-side with a warning and server-side as the real limit.

## Test plan
- Unit: reducer (every command), port compatibility wiring, dirty-state guard, flag gating, RBAC route guard.
- Component/Storybook: every state for CMP-146/152/236/237/238 with visual-regression baselines from D03's fixtures.
- Integration: save path against a mocked then a live backend, incl. the 409/version-conflict branch.
- E2E (Playwright, extended in E37-Q02): author-and-save happy path; refused incompatible connection; viewer 403.
- a11y: axe on the editor route; assert nodes/ports/edges are real focusable DOM elements (a structural test, since the whole keyboard strategy depends on it).
- perf: 200-node fixture pan/zoom benchmark (fuller measurement in E37-Q04).
- Coverage: >=80% frontend.

Threats: elevation of privilege (a viewer or an out-of-scope manager reaching the editor or a rule for an account they cannot trade — mitigated by route guard plus server-side `rules:read`/`rules:write` with `granted_accounts` scoping, and asserted by a test); tampering (client-built model diverging from stored IR — mitigated because the server compiles authoritatively and the client hash is advisory); repudiation (every save emits the audited `rule.graph_saved`); DoS (node/edge caps). Mandatory in this story (not deferred): nodes, ports and edges are real focusable DOM elements with accessible names; the canvas region is a labelled ARIA landmark ("Rule builder canvas" per `05-accessibility-standard.md`); the palette's select+`Enter` insertion path exists; focus rings use CMP-035's shared utility; minimap is `aria-hidden`; target sizes meet §4. Full keyboard authoring, roving tabindex and announcements are completed in E37-S05 and audited in E37-Q05.

Budget: 200 nodes at 60 fps pan/zoom on reference hardware (SCR-082); edge routing memoised; node re-render limited to changed nodes; compile+diff <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node graph and only on save/mode switch. The editor route is lazily code-split so budget #9 (<=8 MB gz initial bundle) is unaffected — asserted by the bundle-size CI check.

title: Implement the node library and inspector over the rule vocabulary
body:
## Context
The canvas from E37-S01 is only useful once nodes carry real semantics. This story implements the five node types named in `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-147 TriggerNode, CMP-148 ConditionNode, CMP-149 ActionNode, CMP-150 LogicGateNode, CMP-151 CommentNode — plus CMP-153 NodeInspectorDrawer, all driven by the closed vocabulary served by `GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary`, which `22-api-openapi.yaml` describes as the single response both editors render their palettes from ("which is what keeps the two editors round-trip compatible").

This covers the graph rendering of **US-RULE-002** (metric vocabulary: units, descriptions, disabled-when-unavailable, `(estimated)` badging) and **US-RULE-003** (action vocabulary: scope declaration, permission-gated actions available only in simulate mode).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-147 TriggerNode**: `on_price_update`, `on_bar_close`, `on_order_fill`, `on_timer`, `on_indicator` with timeframe where applicable; exactly one trigger per rule enforced with a clear message on a second insertion.
- **CMP-148 ConditionNode**: metric + operator + value/reference, using CMP-157 MetricPickerCombobox for the metric; typed output port; displays the metric's unit; renders `(estimated)` as text for heuristic metrics (`iceberg_present_at_level`, `distance_to_liquidity_cluster`, `in_stop_hunt_zone`, `stop_run_detected`, `market_regime`) per US-RULE-002 and CMP-227 EstimatedBadge conventions.
- **CMP-150 LogicGateNode**: `AND` / `OR` / `NOT` with variable input count; the graph-native expression of what the form editor models implicitly; plus `n_of` where the vocabulary exposes it (a graph-only construct, badged as such via `packages/rule-graph`'s `isFormRepresentable`).
- **CMP-149 ActionNode**: the full action vocabulary (`place_order`, `modify_stop_loss`, `modify_take_profit`, `cancel_order`, `move_to_breakeven`, `scale_out`, `scale_in`, `flatten_all_positions`, `halt_new_orders`, `resume_new_orders`, `send_notification`, `log_journal_tag`, `reduce_leverage`, `widen_stop`, `arm_chase_limit`, `start_iceberg_slice`); each node shows the action's declared scope (which accounts/positions it may affect) per US-RULE-003; `flatten_all_positions` requires the explicit acknowledgement documented for SCR-081; order-placing actions are offered to a manager without live-arming permission in simulate-only framing with the restriction explained, and are absent from the palette entirely for accounts the user cannot trade.
- **CMP-151 CommentNode**: free text, non-executable, stored in the presentation block only (never affects the canonical hash).
- **CMP-153 NodeInspectorDrawer**: opened with `Enter` on a focused node (the keyboard contract in CMP-146), hosting dense parameter editing per node type so canvas chrome stays minimal; inspector edits must not trigger a re-layout (SCR-082 §Performance).
- **CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice** mounted non-dismissibly in this editor, with the presence test that fails if it is removed from the composition.
- Unavailable-metric handling per US-RULE-002: a metric requiring recorded data the symbol lacks is shown disabled with the missing dependency named and a one-click action to start recording.
- Storybook stories exactly as listed in the component catalogue for CMP-147..151, CMP-153.

## Out of scope
- Validation/diagnostic rendering and the blocking-save logic → **E37-S03**.
- Round-trip indicator, editor switching, the "What won't round-trip" panel → **E37-S04**.
- Keyboard node-list authoring and announcements → **E37-S05**.
- Any change to the vocabulary itself, the metric registry or action semantics → **E35**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The whole vocabulary is reachable on canvas
  Given GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary
  When the palette and the metric picker are opened
  Then every metric and every action in the response is reachable with its unit and description, and nothing is hard-coded in the client

Scenario: Estimated metrics are badged as text
  Given a heuristic metric such as stop_run_detected
  When it is selected in a condition node
  Then "(estimated)" appears as text on the node and in the rule summary, not as colour or an icon alone

Scenario: Unavailable metric is explained, not hidden
  Given a metric requiring recorded data the symbol lacks
  Then the option is disabled, the missing dependency is named, and a one-click start-recording action is offered

Scenario: A forbidden action is not silently offered (security edge)
  Given a manager without live-arming permission
  Then order-placing actions appear only in simulate framing with the restriction explained, and actions scoped to accounts they cannot trade are not listed at all; a crafted save containing one is rejected by the server with 403

Scenario: Second trigger is refused (error)
  When a second trigger node is inserted
  Then insertion is refused with a message naming the existing trigger, and the graph remains valid

Scenario: Inspector editing does not disturb the layout (edge)
  Given a node positioned by hand
  When its parameters are edited in the inspector drawer
  Then no auto-layout runs, positions are unchanged, and the canonical hash changes only if a semantic parameter changed
```

## Technical notes / design
Node components are thin renderers over `GraphNode.data`; all semantics (allowed operators per metric type, parameter shapes, port types) come from the vocabulary response, cached per session. The `(estimated)` flag, units and permission requirements are vocabulary fields — the client must not maintain its own list, because `22-api-openapi.yaml` states the vocabulary is what keeps the two editors compatible. Comment nodes are written into `GraphLayout.comments` by `packages/rule-graph`, never into the IR. Action scope display reads the account/trade-group scope on the rule (US-RULE-007) and the action's own declared scope.

## Test plan
- Unit: one case per node type render+edit; vocabulary-driven operator filtering; estimated badging; unavailable-metric state; single-trigger enforcement; forbidden-action filtering by permission; comment nodes excluded from the hash.
- Component/Storybook: every story in the catalogue lists for CMP-147..151, CMP-153, with visual-regression baselines.
- Contract: the client renders correctly for the full published vocabulary fixture; a new vocabulary entry appears without a client change (asserted with an extended fixture).
- Integration: inspector edit → compile → IR reflects the change; comment/position edits → hash unchanged.
- a11y: axe on each node type and the inspector drawer; accessible names match the CMP-147/148 patterns ("Trigger node: on bar close, 5m").
- Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
This story is where privilege boundaries become visible in the UI. Threats: elevation of privilege (authoring an action against an account the user cannot trade), spoofing of safety posture (an emulated stop presented as if it replaced the native exchange SL). title: Surface validation, cycles, orphans and diagnostics on the offending node

## Context
US-RULE-005 requires that "the graph validates continuously and errors are shown on the offending node", that cycles are refused with the offending path highlighted, and that orphan/dangling nodes are warnings on canvas but blocking errors on save, listed by node name in a jump-to-node error list. CMP-234 ValidationPanel is the shared surface for **both** editors and has a contract test of its own: the same IR must produce identical diagnostics in form and graph modes (`15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-234 §Data contract).

Diagnostics come from the server (`POST /api/v1/rules/validate` over the compiled IR) so that what the editor shows is exactly what the engine will enforce; local analysis from `packages/rule-graph` (cycles, dangling ports, orphans, form-subset) supplies instant feedback for structural problems the server would also reject.

## Scope / Deliverables
- CMP-234 ValidationPanel mounted in graph mode with `anchor.kind = "node" | "edge"`; `role="log"`, errors first, error count announced on every recompile; each entry is a button that moves focus to the offending node/edge — the sole keyboard mechanism for navigating graph diagnostics.
- Local structural analysis wired from `packages/rule-graph`: `findCycles` (highlight the whole cycle path on canvas and enumerate it in the panel), `findOrphans` (nodes reaching no action — warning on canvas, blocking on save), `findDanglingPorts` (required inputs unconnected — same treatment).
- Server validation on save and on demand (`Validate` action, `Ctrl+Enter`): compile via `POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile`, validate via `POST /rules/validate`, render returned `RuleValidationIssue`s anchored to nodes.
- On-canvas error/warning treatment per node and per edge (text + glyph, never colour-only), plus the header error/warning counters shown in the SCR-082 footer strip ("errors: 0").
- Save blocking: a graph with any error cannot be saved as anything but a draft, and can never be armed; arming entry points are disabled with the reason stated in text.
- Quarantine handling (US-RULE-001): a stored IR failing schema validation loads read-only and force-disarmed, names the failing JSON path, offers export-as-JSON, and is never partially rendered as editable.
- Engine-unavailable state: `POST /rules/validate` unreachable → the `Not verified` posture, draft-save only, arming blocked, stated in text (never silently "valid").

## Out of scope
- The round-trip indicator's four states and the mismatch diff → **E37-S04** (this story provides the diagnostics plumbing it reuses).
- Backend validation rules themselves → **E35**. Rule conflict/precedence detection across rules (US-RULE-011) → **E35/E36** surfaces; this story only renders CMP-159 RuleConflictWarning if the save response contains conflicts.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An error is shown on the offending node
  Given a condition node missing its value
  When validation runs
  Then the node renders an error treatment with text, the ValidationPanel lists the issue anchored to that node, and activating the entry moves focus to it

Scenario: A cycle is refused and drawn as a path
  When I connect a node output back into one of its own upstream inputs
  Then the connection is refused, the cycle is highlighted as a path on canvas and enumerated in the panel, and no IR containing a cycle is ever produced

Scenario: Orphans warn on canvas and block on save
  Given nodes reaching no action node and a required input left unconnected
  Then both are warnings while editing, and attempting to save raises blocking errors listing each node by its accessible name with a jump-to-node action

Scenario: Both editors report identical diagnostics (contract)
  Given one rule IR
  When it is validated from the form editor and from the graph editor
  Then the returned diagnostics are identical in set and severity, anchored to the corresponding row and node respectively

Scenario: Validation service unavailable (failure)
  Given POST /rules/validate is unreachable
  Then the editor shows "Not verified" in text, permits draft save only, blocks arming, and never presents the graph as valid

Scenario: Quarantined rule (error edge)
  Given a stored IR that fails schema validation
  Then the rule opens read-only and force-disarmed, the failing JSON path is named, export-as-JSON is offered, and no partial execution or partial editing is possible
```

## Technical notes / design
Diagnostic pipeline: local analysis runs on every graph mutation (cheap, structural) and is merged with server diagnostics (authoritative, semantic) into one list keyed by `{severity, anchor}`; on conflict the server wins. Debounce local analysis to one run per animation frame. Compile+validate runs on save and on mode switch (SCR-082 §Performance), plus explicitly via `Ctrl+Enter`; it must not run per keystroke. Error counts are announced through a single polite live region, coalesced per recompile (per E37-D04's announcement-coalescing rule).

## Test plan
- Unit: merge logic (local vs server precedence), debounce, save-blocking predicate, arming-disabled predicate, quarantine branch, engine-unavailable branch.
- Component: CMP-234 stories Valid/WithErrors/WithWarnings/GraphAnchored, focus-to-anchor interaction test in graph mode.
- Contract: **same IR ⇒ same diagnostics in both editors** (the named CMP-234 contract test), run against the live validate endpoint.
- Integration: cycle, orphan, dangling, missing-value and type-mismatch fixtures each producing the specified UI state.
- E2E: validate-blocked save; unreachable-service posture.
- a11y: `role="log"` semantics, focus movement on anchor activation, announcement coalescing, non-colour error encoding.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Validation shown in the UI must never be more permissive than the server's: a test asserts a graph the client believes valid is still rejected if the server disagrees, and that the UI then blocks rather than retries silently. Quarantine exists precisely to stop a hand-edited or truncated IR from being partially executed (tampering/integrity). Arming remains impossible from this editor; the arming entry point only routes to SCR-085's step-up flow.

## Accessibility notes
The ValidationPanel is the keyboard user's map of the graph: `role="log"`, errors first, every entry focus-moving, error count announced once per recompile. On-canvas error state must be text+glyph. This is the mechanism `05-accessibility-standard.md` §5 requires so canvas-only information does not exist.

## Performance notes
Local analysis <=5 ms per mutation on a 200-node graph (it runs on every edit); compile+validate round trip <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node graph and only on save/mode switch/explicit validate.

## Observability
Analytics `rule.graph_validation_run {errors,warnings,durationMs}`, `rule.graph_cycle_rejected`, `rule.graph_save_blocked {reason}`; metric `rule_graph_validation_duration_ms`; error logs carry the `RuleGraphError` codes. The audited `rule.validated` event is emitted server-side.

title: Implement round-trip switching, the four-state indicator and the mismatch diff
body:
## Context
This story delivers the graph side of **US-RULE-006** and the product promise behind owner decision #11: a rule may be opened in either editor, and switching must never change what it does. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.3 makes this R3 exit criterion 5 ("a corpus of >=30 rules authored in the form editor opens in the node editor and returns to the form editor with an identical IR ... and vice versa"), and US-RULE-006's NFR states the hash comparison "runs in production, not only in tests".

`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-082 specifies the mirrored four-state indicator in detail; E36 implements the form side. Both read the same `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile` response.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-235 EditorModeToggle** in graph mode with the four indicator states: `Round-trips ✓` · `Unsupported in form view` · `Round-trip mismatch` · `Not verified`, each rendered as text+glyph with its specified tooltip/panel.
- **"What won't round-trip" panel**: clickable from the `Unsupported in form view` state; lists each offending node by its accessible name, why it cannot be represented in the form (nested sub-graph, fan-out edge feeding two actions, nested arithmetic, `n_of`, multi-level nesting), and what the form editor will show instead (a read-only summary card). Offending nodes are additionally badged on canvas with a non-colour glyph **and** enumerated in the `Alt+L` node list so the warning is never canvas-only.
- **Graph-only construct marking at creation time** (US-RULE-005 edge scenario): the moment a node-only construct is created — e.g. fanning one output into two consumers — the node is badged, the rule header shows "contains node-only constructs", and this is recorded in the IR so the form editor renders it read-only rather than discovering it at switch time.
- **Hash proof on every switch** (US-RULE-006): switching without editing compares the canonical `ir_hash` before and after; on difference the switch is **aborted**, the rule is left untouched, a "round-trip integrity failure" error is raised showing both hashes with a downloadable diff, and a high-severity telemetry event is emitted.
- **`Round-trip mismatch` resolution UI**: saving and arming blocked; the diff rendered (reusing SCR-088's diff renderer) with the diverging node selected on canvas and focused in the node list; exactly two explicit recovery choices — "Keep the form version (the graph layout will be regenerated)" / "Keep the graph version (discard form edits)" — each restating what is lost; never auto-resolved; the choice is audited.
- **Switch-while-armed** (US-RULE-006): viewing an armed rule in either editor is allowed; the first edit requires either disarming or explicitly choosing "edit as a new draft version", so the running version can never mutate under the runtime.
- **Unsaved-changes prompt** on switch (apply or discard) and **optimistic-concurrency** rejection when the other tab saved a version this editor did not see, naming the other editor and session and offering reload-and-reapply.
- **Migration during a switch**: if the rule was migrated on open (older IR version), comparison is made against the post-migration hash, the migration is recorded once as its own version entry, and the rule stays disarmed until reviewed.
- Presentation preservation: switching to the form editor, editing a threshold and returning must show the original hand-placed layout, not an auto-layout (US-RULE-001 "Presentation data survives the round trip").

## Out of scope
- The form editor's own indicator and read-only summary cards → **E36** (mirrored spec; this story coordinates with it).
- The IR, canonicalisation and the compile endpoint → **E35**; SCR-088 IR inspector itself → E35/E36 (this story reuses its diff renderer).
- The >=30-rule corpus test execution → **E37-Q03** (this story provides the behaviour it verifies).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Switching without editing preserves the IR
  Given a rule open in the graph editor
  When I switch to the form editor and back without editing
  Then the canonical ir_hash is identical at every hop and the indicator reads "Round-trips" throughout

Scenario: A graph-only construct is declared at creation time
  When I fan one node's output into two action nodes
  Then that node is badged immediately, the header states "contains node-only constructs", the fact is recorded in the IR, and the form editor will render that sub-tree read-only

Scenario: Hash proof fails on switch (failure path)
  Given the pre-switch and post-switch canonical hashes differ
  Then the switch is aborted, the rule is untouched, a round-trip integrity failure is shown with both hashes and a downloadable diff, and a high-severity telemetry event is emitted

Scenario: Mismatch is never auto-resolved (error)
  Given the form and graph representations compile to different IR
  Then saving and arming are blocked, the diff is shown with the diverging node selected on canvas and focused in the node list, and only the two explicit recovery choices are offered, each restating what is lost; the chosen resolution is audited

Scenario: Switching an armed rule (edge)
  Given the rule is currently armed
  When I switch editors and then attempt the first edit
  Then I must either disarm or choose "edit as a new draft version", and the armed version is never mutated

Scenario: Layout survives a form-side edit (edge)
  Given a graph with hand-placed node positions
  When I edit a threshold in the form editor and return
  Then my original layout is shown rather than an auto-layout, and the canonical hash changed only because of the threshold

Scenario: Concurrent edit in two tabs (error)
  Given the same rule is open in the form editor in another tab which saves first
  When this editor saves
  Then the save is rejected with an optimistic-concurrency error naming the other editor and session, offering reload-and-reapply, with no last-writer-wins overwrite
```

## Technical notes / design
- Authority: `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile` (`{editor, model}` → `{ir, ir_hash, issues}`) is the only source of the canonical hash. The client mirror in `packages/rule-graph` is used to pre-empt a switch, but a client/server disagreement is itself reported as `Round-trip mismatch` — never resolved locally.
- The four indicator states map 1:1 to the `rule.roundtrip_verified {result}` values `identical | graph_only_construct | mismatch | unverified` defined in `14-screens-catalogue.md`, so the UI state and the audit vocabulary cannot drift.
- `graph_layout` is persisted on the rule version but excluded from the hash (`24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4 guarantee 3), which is what makes "layout survives" and "moving a box creates no new version" simultaneously true.
- Form-subset determination uses `isFormRepresentable` from `packages/rule-graph` for instant marking, confirmed by the server's `issues` on compile.
- Version conflicts use the rule's version/ETag from `GET /rules/{ruleId}`; the reject path must name the other session (available from the WS `rules` topic / conflict response).

## Test plan
- Unit: indicator state machine (all four states + transitions), hash-compare gate, abort-on-mismatch, armed-edit gate, migration path, concurrency rejection.
- Integration: compile round trip against a live backend for form- and graph-authored fixtures; the layout-preservation case; the migration case with an older stored IR version.
- E2E (Playwright): full switch cycle for every construct in the metric/action vocabulary (the explicit requirement in US-RULE-006's NFR), graph-only construct flow, mismatch resolution flow, armed-rule flow, two-tab concurrency flow.
- Chaos-ish: compile endpoint 5xx and timeout → `Not verified`, arming blocked.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
This is a security-relevant story: a silent round-trip change could alter what an armed rule does — an integrity and repudiation threat. Controls: server-authoritative hash; abort-not-repair on mismatch; `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved {choice}` audited because a resolution can silently change an armed rule's behaviour; armed rules are immutable to in-place edits; optimistic concurrency prevents last-writer-wins. A high-severity telemetry event on integrity failure ensures the condition is noticed rather than absorbed by the user. Abuse case coverage in E37-X02.

## Accessibility notes
Indicator states are text+glyph with an accessible name stating the state and its consequence; the "What won't round-trip" panel is a keyboard-reachable list whose entries move focus to the offending node; the mismatch dialog is `role="alertdialog"` restating the loss of each choice in plain language; all badges are enumerated in the `Alt+L` node list so nothing is canvas-only; the switch confirmation before entering a lossy form view is announced.

## Performance notes
Compile+diff completes <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node rule and runs on save and mode switch only (SCR-081/SCR-082 §Performance). The switch must feel immediate: show a determinate pending state rather than blocking the UI while the compile is in flight.

## Observability
`rule.roundtrip_verified {result}` and `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved {choice}` (both audited, server-side), `rule.graph_saved`; high-severity telemetry `rule.roundtrip_integrity_failure {hashBefore,hashAfter,ruleId}`; metrics `rule_graph_roundtrip_mismatch_total` (alerting on any non-zero in staging), `rule_graph_compile_duration_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios covered by named automated tests incl. the per-construct E2E switch matrix.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%; CI green.
- [ ] Security review comment present; audit events verified end-to-end in the audit log.

## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 makes "the node canvas has a verified non-canvas alternative" an R3 quality gate, and §7.3 exit criterion 13 requires "a11y pass incl. the node editor's keyboard alternative". US-RULE-005 carries an explicit keyboard-only-construction scenario as a Must acceptance criterion, and `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146 mandates a three-layer strategy (DOM-mirror nodes, roving-tabindex navigation with keyboard connect, and the form-view toggle as an equal-status alternative). SCR-082's a11y section adds the `Alt+L` node list panel: "the canvas is never the only way to author".

E37-S01 laid down real focusable DOM elements; this story turns them into a complete, announced, keyboard-first authoring path built exactly to the keyboard authoring map signed off in E37-D04.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **`Alt+L` node-list panel**: a linear, non-spatial view of the graph — every node with its accessible name, type, parameters summary and its connections described in text ("ATR 14, output connects to Multiply input A"); add / connect / disconnect / delete / rename / open-inspector affordances as real form controls; diagnostics and node-only badges enumerated here (never canvas-only).
- **Roving tabindex navigation**: `Tab` enters the graph region (a labelled ARIA landmark), arrow keys move between connected nodes, `Enter` opens the node inspector (CMP-153), `F2` renames, `Delete` removes the selection, `Esc` returns focus to the region.
- **Keyboard connect** (CMP-237/CMP-148 contract): focus an output port → `Enter` starts a connection → arrow-select a target port → `Enter` confirms; incompatible targets are *announced as incompatible with the reason string* from `packages/rule-graph`'s port matrix rather than merely being un-droppable; `Esc` cancels the pending connection.
- **Keyboard edge handling**: an edge is reachable (node → `Tab` to its edges, or from the node list), selectable, and deletable with `Delete`, with "Delete connection" also exposed in its context menu (CMP-152 contract).
- **Non-drag node insertion** completed end-to-end: palette entry selected + `Enter` inserts and connects to the current selection where types allow (the pointer-free path from CMP-236).
- **Live-region announcements**: one polite announcement per completed operation (node added, connection made naming both endpoints, connection refused with reason, node deleted, auto-layout applied, error count after recompile), coalesced per E37-D04's rule so rapid editing does not flood.
- **Shared undo/redo**: keyboard-initiated edits use the same command stack as pointer edits (US-RULE-005: "the same undo/redo stack applies as for pointer edits").
- **Form-view toggle as equal status**: wording and placement per E37-D04, presented as an alternative rather than a fallback.
- Reduced-motion support: edge animation disabled; focus movement without animated transit.

## Out of scope
- The a11y *audit* of the result → **E37-Q05**. Design of the keyboard map → **E37-D04**.
- Auto-layout, node search and minimap → **E37-T02** (this story consumes their keyboard entry points).
- The form editor's own keyboard completeness → **E36**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Build a complete rule without a pointer
  Given a user who never uses a pointer
  When they add a trigger, a condition, a logic gate and an action from the keyboard palette, connect them via the port keyboard-connect flow, edit parameters in the inspector and save
  Then a valid rule is produced, identical in IR to the same rule built by pointer

Scenario: A connection is announced
  When a connection is completed by keyboard
  Then a live region announces "connected CVD divergence output to AND input 1", naming both endpoints

Scenario: An incompatible target is announced, not merely ignored (error)
  When a boolean output is aimed at a numeric input by keyboard
  Then the attempt is refused and the announcement states the incompatibility and its reason, and focus remains on the pending connection so another target can be chosen

Scenario: Every canvas operation exists in the node list (a11y gate)
  Given the operation inventory from E37-D04's keyboard authoring map
  When each row is exercised through the Alt+L panel
  Then every operation completes, with zero operations reachable only on canvas

Scenario: Undo is shared (edge)
  Given a mix of pointer and keyboard edits
  When Ctrl+Z is pressed repeatedly
  Then edits unwind in a single chronological order regardless of input modality

Scenario: Announcement flooding is prevented (edge)
  When ten nodes are added in rapid succession
  Then announcements are coalesced per the agreed rule rather than queueing ten separate messages
```

## Technical notes / design
Keyboard commands dispatch the same reducer commands as pointer interactions (E37-S01), so behaviour cannot diverge; this is asserted by a test that builds the same rule through both paths and compares canonical hashes. The node list renders from `GraphModel` + diagnostics, so it is automatically complete as new node types are added. Announcements use a single `aria-live="polite"` region with a coalescing queue; errors use `role="alert"` sparingly (blocking conditions only). ## Test plan
- Unit: command parity (keyboard vs pointer command dispatch), announcement coalescing, focus return, roving tabindex model.
- Interaction tests (named CI gate per CMP-146 §Tests): keyboard node navigation, keyboard connect incl. type rejection with a spoken reason, keyboard edge delete, keyboard-only node insertion.
- E2E: the full "build a rule with the keyboard only" journey, asserting the resulting IR hash equals the pointer-built equivalent.
- a11y: axe on the editor and the node-list panel; manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes against E37-D04's screen-reader script, recorded.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
No new data paths. One safety property is asserted here: **no keyboard shortcut arms a rule** — arming always routes to SCR-085's step-up flow, so the keyboard map cannot be used to bypass 2FA. A test asserts the editor registers no binding that reaches `PUT /rules/{ruleId}/mode` directly.

## Accessibility notes
This story is the accessibility deliverable of the epic: WCAG 2.2 AA with particular attention to 2.1.1 Keyboard (no trap), 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.5.8 Target Size, 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value and 4.1.3 Status Messages. ## Performance notes
Node-list rendering is virtualised above 50 rows (CMP-049 convention) so a 200-node graph does not stall; announcement coalescing bounds live-region churn; keyboard navigation must respond within one frame.

Analytics `rule.graph_keyboard_authoring_used` (the adoption signal specified in E37-D04), `rule.graph_keyboard_connect_rejected {fromType,toType}`; no new audit events.

## Context
US-RULE-005 requires an auto-layout that "arranges nodes without changing semantics" and is undoable, and SCR-082 lists `Ctrl+L` auto-layout, a minimap and node search among its interactions. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §12 lists "Node-editor auto-layout and node search — E37" as a **descoping candidate** deferrable to R5, so this task is deliberately separated from the core authoring stories: if the train runs hot, this is what slips, and nothing else in E37 depends on it beyond graceful degradation.

E37-K01 decides whether layout runs on the main thread or in a worker.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Auto-layout (`Ctrl+L`) using the layout library chosen in E37-K01 (elkjs or dagre), operating on `GraphModel` and producing only a new `GraphLayout` — semantics and therefore the canonical IR hash are provably untouched.
- Undo support for auto-layout as a single command on the shared stack, plus the explicit undo affordance if E37-D01 found one necessary.
- Layout for rules that arrive with no `graph_layout` (i.e. authored in the form editor and opened in the graph editor for the first time) — the default entry path for most rules.
- Node search: filter/jump by node name, metric or action id, with keyboard-first results that move focus to the node and are mirrored in the `Alt+L` list.
- CMP-238 Minimap behaviour: viewport tracking, click/drag to navigate, error-node markers; `aria-hidden` with the node list as its documented equivalent.
- Degradation: if layout would exceed its time budget (very large graphs), run it in a worker or chunk it, and show a determinate progress affordance rather than freezing.

## Out of scope
- Canvas, nodes, ports, edges (E37-S01/S02); keyboard authoring (E37-S05); validation (E37-S03).
- Persisting layout — already handled by `packages/rule-graph`'s `GraphLayout` and the rule version document.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Auto-layout never changes semantics
  Given any graph
  When Ctrl+L is pressed
  Then the canonical IR hash before and after is identical, and only node positions change

Scenario: Auto-layout is undoable as one step
  When Ctrl+Z follows an auto-layout
  Then every node returns to its previous position in a single undo step

Scenario: A form-authored rule opens laid out
  Given a rule authored in the form editor with no stored graph_layout
  When it is opened in the graph editor
  Then a readable layout is generated automatically, with no overlapping nodes and no crossing edges beyond what the graph structurally requires

Scenario: Large-graph budget (performance edge)
  Given a 200-node graph
  When auto-layout runs
  Then the main thread is not blocked beyond 100 ms, the animated transition completes within 400 ms total, and the reduced-motion variant repositions without transit

Scenario: Search jumps and announces
  When a node is located by search and activated
  Then focus moves to that node, the viewport centres on it, and the move is announced
```

## Technical notes / design
Layout runs as a pure function `layout(graph): GraphLayout`; the result is applied through the same reducer command used by manual moves so undo works without special casing. Worker placement is decided by E37-K01's ADR; if used, the worker is bundled with the lazily-loaded editor route. Layout direction is left-to-right (trigger → conditions → action) matching the SCR-082 wireframe. Minimap is derived state, memoised, and re-rendered at most at animation-frame cadence.

## Test plan
- Unit: hash-invariance of layout over the fixture corpus; undo as a single command; deterministic layout output for a given graph (golden fixture) so visual-regression is stable.
- Performance: 60-node and 200-node layout timings (wall clock, main-thread block) asserted against the budgets, run in the perf suite from E37-Q04.
- Interaction: search → focus → announce; minimap navigation with a pointer.
- a11y: assert the minimap is `aria-hidden` and that search results are keyboard reachable and mirrored in the node list.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
N/A — presentation-only computation on data already in the client. One integrity assertion is included: layout must not be able to alter the IR, and the hash-invariance test is the proof.

## Accessibility notes
Auto-layout and search must be reachable from the keyboard and from the `Alt+L` node list; auto-layout is announced once on completion; reduced-motion removes transit. The minimap is explicitly a pointer convenience with documented equivalents, per CMP-238.

## Performance notes
Budgets: main-thread block <=100 ms at 200 nodes, animated transition <=400 ms total (D03 motion cap), minimap re-render within the frame budget, no layout on inspector edits.

## Observability
Analytics `rule.graph_autolayout_used {nodeCount,durationMs}`, `rule.graph_search_used`; metric `rule_graph_layout_duration_ms`.

body:
## Context
> **Classification note.** This is a documentation/ADR reconciliation chore (kind `Chore`, mirroring E36-T02), not net-new delivery engineering. It is excluded from the E37 delivery-engineering subtotal reconciled against the roadmap's 26-point epic estimate; see "Estimate reconciliation" in the E37 epic body.

ADR-0007 fixed the single-IR decision before the node editor existed; it states that graphs "must be acyclic and must reduce to a single boolean condition plus an ordered action list" and that layout lives in `meta.layout`. Implementation in E37-S04 pins down details ADR-0007 left open: exactly which constructs are graph-only, how they are marked *at creation time*, how round-trip integrity failures behave in production, and the audit vocabulary (`identical | graph_only_construct | mismatch | unverified`). `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires docs to reflect shipped behaviour, not the original proposal.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR-0007 addendum** (appended to `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md`, or ADR-00xx superseding-in-part if the change is material): the definitive graph-only construct list (nested arithmetic, `n_of`, boolean nesting deeper than the two-level form subset, an output fanning into multiple consumers, nested sub-graphs), the creation-time marking rule, the production hash-comparison behaviour (abort, never repair), and the resolution-choice audit.
- Update `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4 where implementation clarified the round-trip guarantees (notably the presentation block's exact contents and its exclusion from the hash).
- Update `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-082 and `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146..153 / CMP-234..238 to match shipped props, states, hotkeys and a11y behaviour.
- A short **rule-authoring guide** section for the user-facing docs: when to use the graph vs the form editor, what "node-only" means for your rule, how to read the four round-trip states, and the complete keyboard authoring map (from E37-D04) as a printable reference.
- A changelog fragment for the R3 release describing the node editor and its feature flag.

## Out of scope
- Rewriting the IR specification itself (E35 owns §11.1–§11.3, §11.5, §11.6).
- Marketing/tutorial content; video walkthroughs.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR matches shipped behaviour
  Given the implemented graph-only construct detection
  When the ADR addendum is reviewed against packages/rule-graph's isFormRepresentable
  Then the construct list in the ADR and the code's detection set are identical, with a test referencing the ADR list as its fixture

Scenario: Catalogue entries match the build
  Given SCR-082 and CMP-146..153/234..238 entries
  When compared with the shipped screen and component props
  Then states, hotkeys, props and a11y contracts match, and any divergence is corrected in the docs rather than left stale

Scenario: The keyboard map is published
  Then the complete keyboard authoring map appears in the user-facing guide and matches the bindings registered in the app, verified by a test that enumerates registered bindings against the documented list

Scenario: A divergence cannot be resolved (failure)
  Given shipped behaviour that contradicts a locked plan decision
  Then it is escalated to the Architect and either the code or the decision is changed, never silently documented as-is
```

## Technical notes / design
Prefer an addendum over a new ADR unless the decision changed materially; ADR-0007's "Consequences" section gains the graph-only list. The binding-enumeration test is a small unit test in the web app that asserts the registered hotkey table equals the documented one — this is how the docs stay true.

## Test plan
Docs lint/link check in CI; the ADR-construct-list fixture test; the hotkey-enumeration test. No runtime behaviour changes.
