title: Build the >=30-rule round-trip corpus and the IR fuzz gate (R3 exit criterion 5)
body:
## Context
R3 exit criterion 5 (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.3) is explicit: "a corpus of >=30 rules authored in the form editor opens in the node editor and returns to the form editor with an identical IR (byte-equal serialisation) and vice versa". US-RULE-001's NFR adds a property-based requirement: ">=10 000 generated documents per CI run assert round-trip equality across form→IR→node→IR→form", and US-RULE-006's NFR calls the equivalence release-blocking. This ticket builds the corpus, the generator and the CI gate that make those claims checkable rather than asserted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Corpus**: >=30 real rules covering the full metric and action vocabulary and every construct class — simple comparison, two-level `all_of`/`any_of`, `n_of`, each temporal operator (`sustained_for`, `occurred_within`, `count_within`, `stable_for`), nested arithmetic, fan-out to two actions, comment nodes, multi-action lists, scoped rules, and every action in the vocabulary at least once. Authored roughly half in the form editor and half in the graph editor. Checked into `packages/fixtures` with each rule's expected canonical hash.
- **Round-trip gate**: an automated test that, for each corpus rule, performs form→graph→form and graph→form→graph, asserting the canonical `ir_hash` from `POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile` is unchanged at every hop, and that graph-only rules fail *loudly* (render read-only in the form) rather than silently degrading.
- **Property/fuzz generator**: generates valid IR documents from the published JSON Schema (`GET /api/v1/schemas/rule-ir.json`), biased to include deep nesting, boundary child counts (1 and 32, the schema's `maxItems`), extreme numeric formats (`1.50` vs `1.5`), unusual key insertion order and node-id orderings — asserting hash stability across every hop, per the US-RULE-001 fuzz scenario. >=10 000 documents per CI run.
- **Presentation-invariance test**: randomised layout mutations (positions, collapsed state, comment text) must never change the canonical hash; and a form-side edit must never destroy the layout.
- CI wiring as a **required check** on any PR touching `packages/rule-graph`, the rule editors or the IR schema; failures report the offending document with a minimised reproduction.

## Out of scope
- The compiler/canonicalisation implementation itself (E35) and the adapter (E37-T01) — this ticket tests them.
- Functional UI E2E (E37-Q02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Exit criterion 5 is demonstrably met
  Given the corpus of at least 30 rules
  When each is round-tripped in both directions
  Then every canonical ir_hash is unchanged, and the run output is attached to E37 as the evidence for R3 exit criterion 5

Scenario: The fuzz gate runs at the mandated volume
  Then at least 10000 generated documents are round-tripped per CI run, within the CI time budget, with the seed recorded so any failure is reproducible

Scenario: A lossy hop fails loudly (failure path)
  Given a document that one editor cannot represent
  Then the hop raises a named error and the test asserts the loud failure, rather than passing because an approximate document was emitted

Scenario: Cosmetic changes never create a version (edge)
  Given randomised position, collapse and comment mutations
  Then the canonical hash is unchanged for every mutation, and no new rule_versions row is created by a layout-only save

Scenario: A regression is caught in CI (proof)
  Given a deliberately introduced canonicalisation change (e.g. number formatting)
  Then the gate fails and names the first diverging document with a minimised reproduction
```

## Technical notes / design
The generator uses the published schema so it cannot drift from the backend. Shrinking/minimisation is required: a failure must produce the smallest document that still fails, otherwise triage is impractical at 10 000 documents. Corpus hashes are stored as golden files, so a change to canonicalisation is visible as a reviewable diff rather than a silent pass. Runs against a live backend for the authoritative compile, with the client mirror checked in the same run.

## Test plan
This ticket is a test asset. Its own verification: the deliberate-regression scenario above, plus reviewing that the corpus covers every construct class (a coverage table checked in beside the fixtures).

## Security notes
Integrity-focused: this gate is the primary defence against a rule silently changing meaning between editors — the tampering/integrity threat in E37-X01's model. Corpus rules use demo accounts and contain no secrets. Generated documents are bounded by the schema's own limits so the fuzz run cannot be used as a DoS against the backend compile endpoint (rate-limited and run against a dedicated CI backend).

## Accessibility notes
N/A (headless gate). It does, however, verify the property that makes the form editor a legitimate accessible alternative to the canvas: a rule truly is the same rule in both editors.

## Performance notes

title: Benchmark the 200-node 60 fps and 500 ms compile+diff budgets
body:
## Context
SCR-082 states two hard numbers: **200 nodes at 60 fps**, and the round-trip **compile + diff check within 500 ms p95 for a 100-node graph**, with "edge routing memoised" and "inspector edits do not re-layout the graph". `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §1 requires every number to be a testable budget with a defined measurement method and a CI regression gate — not an aspiration. E37-K01 measured a prototype; this ticket measures the shipped editor and gates it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Benchmark harness (promoted from E37-K01's if suitable) measuring, on the reference hardware in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1, in Electron and Chromium:
  1. Pan/zoom frame time p50/p95 on the 200-node/~260-edge fixture (60 s exercise).
  2. Frame time at 60 nodes (the common case) and at whatever node cap E37-K01's ADR set.
  3. Auto-layout wall clock and main-thread block time at 60 and 200 nodes.
  4. Compile+diff round-trip p95 on the 100-node fixture (client + network + server), measured on save and on mode switch.
  5. Inspector-edit cost: assert no layout pass runs and that only the edited node re-renders.
  6. Editor route bundle size (gzipped) and confirmation it is code-split out of the initial bundle (budget #9).
  7. Memory over a 30-minute editing soak on the 200-node graph (no unbounded growth from undo stack or memoised edges).
- Comparison of every result against its budget, recorded in the perf results log with the method and hardware stated.
- CI regression gate: frame-time and compile p95 thresholds tracked per commit with an alert at the agreed regression margin; bundle size tracked per `06` §8.

## Out of scope
- Backend rule-engine evaluation performance (E35), API/WS load testing (E34/E29 own the k6 profiles).
- Functional correctness (E37-Q02) and a11y (E37-Q05).

```gherkin
Scenario: The 200-node budget is measured, not assumed

  When pan and zoom are exercised for 60 seconds
  Then p50 and p95 frame times are recorded and compared against 16.6 ms, and the result is either within budget or raised as a blocking finding against E37-S01/T02

Scenario: Compile+diff meets its p95
  Given the 100-node fixture
  When save and mode switch are exercised 100 times
  Then p95 of the compile+diff round trip is <=500 ms and the breakdown (client adapter / network / server compile) is recorded

Scenario: Inspector edits do not re-layout (edge)
  When a node parameter is edited in the inspector
  Then no layout pass is observed and re-render is confined to the edited node, asserted programmatically rather than by eye

Scenario: A budget is missed (failure path)
  Given any measured value exceeding its budget
  Then a blocking finding is filed against the owning ticket, and either the code is fixed or the documented node cap in SCR-082 and ADR from E37-K01 is revised with Architect sign-off — never quietly accepted

Scenario: Memory does not grow without bound (edge)
  Given a 30-minute editing soak on the 200-node graph
  Then resident memory returns to a stable plateau after undo-stack trimming, with no monotonic growth
```

## Technical notes / design
Measurement method per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7: `requestAnimationFrame` timestamps plus the Performance panel for the worst frame; deterministic scripted pan/zoom so runs are comparable; three repetitions with the median reported. N/A — local fixtures, demo backend. The bundle measurement includes an SCA check that no new transitive dependency entered with the layout/graph libraries since E37-K01.

## Accessibility notes
The reduced-motion path is measured too (auto-layout without transit must be at least as fast), so the accessible path is never the slow path.

## Performance notes
Budgets asserted: frame time <=16.6 ms p95 at 200 nodes (never below the 30 fps floor), auto-layout main-thread block <=100 ms, compile+diff <=500 ms p95 at 100 nodes, editor route lazily loaded (budget #9 unaffected), stable memory over a 30-minute soak.

Results published to the perf dashboard with the same metric names the app emits (`rule_graph_compile_duration_ms`, `rule_graph_layout_duration_ms`) so production telemetry and lab numbers are directly comparable.

- [ ] All seven measurements recorded with method, hardware and both shells stated.
- [ ] Results compared against budgets; findings filed for any miss with an owner.
- [ ] CI regression gate wired with agreed thresholds.
- [ ] Results attached to E37 for the epic's perf DoD item and referenced in the PRR pack.

body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass, not just child-ticket QA, before an Epic can be Done; §8 states QA sign-off is never silently skipped. Scripted tests (E37-Q02/Q03) cover what we thought of; this ticket covers what we did not — a graph editor is exactly the kind of surface where unusual sequences (paste, rapid undo, switching editors mid-connection) find defects.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charters** (session-based, 90 min each, minimum four):
  1. *Break the round-trip*: try to make the editors disagree — switch mid-edit, mid-connection, during a pending compile, with a migrated rule, with the engine offline, with two tabs racing.
  2. *Abuse the graph*: maximum node/edge counts, deep nesting, self-referencing attempts, deleting a node mid-connection, undo across a save, paste of a foreign rule document.
  3. *Mixed-modality authoring*: alternate pointer and keyboard on the same rule; interleave the node list and canvas; verify one undo history and one announcement stream.
  4. *Permission and environment edges*: manager without live-arming, viewer, an account removed from scope while the editor is open, kill-switch engaged mid-edit, feature flag toggled mid-session.
- Session notes with a defect list, each triaged to an owning ticket with a priority; P0/P1 defects fixed before the epic closes.
- **Regression pack additions**: the node-editor cases from E37-Q01 that must run before every future release, merged into the product regression pack with clear pass criteria (including the round-trip gate, the keyboard map matrix and the perf thresholds as referenced gates rather than duplicated work).
- **QA sign-off comment** on E37 and on each story, with pass/fail per plan scenario and any recorded deviations.

## Out of scope
- Writing the scripted plan (E37-Q01), automating it (E37-Q02), the corpus gate (E37-Q03), perf (E37-Q04), a11y audit (E37-Q05) — this ticket consumes all of them.
- Security abuse cases (E37-X02), though findings are cross-referenced.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  When the sessions are complete
  Then each charter has session notes, a coverage statement and a defect list, with every defect triaged to an owning ticket and a priority

The node editor authors documents that, once armed, place and cancel real orders through the rule engine (C10 → OMS). `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 names E35 in the R3 STRIDE list; E37 is its authoring surface and inherits the same exposure with its own client-side twist: a rich client model compiled into an executable document.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE model over the editor's data flow: browser editor state → `POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile` → `POST /rules/validate` → `PUT /rules/{ruleId}` → `rule_versions` → (later) arming via `PUT /rules/{ruleId}/mode` → engine execution → OMS actions. Trust boundaries drawn explicitly (browser ↔ API, API ↔ engine, engine ↔ OMS).

- Risk rating (likelihood × impact) per threat, with existing controls named and gaps recorded as actionable items assigned to E37 stories or E35.
- Explicit verification that the presentation block (`graph_layout`, comments, collapsed state) cannot carry semantics — i.e. that nothing in it can influence evaluation — since it is excluded from the canonical hash and therefore from the integrity guarantee.
- Confirmation of the arming boundary: no path from this editor sets `mode` without the SCR-085 step-up flow.
- Feed into `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` for any new or retired risk.

## Out of scope
- The rule engine's own runtime threat model, sandboxing and execution budget (E35); OMS and fan-out models (E29/E34).

```gherkin

  Then each of the six categories has at least one enumerated, rated threat with named controls or a recorded gap, and no category is dismissed without a written reason

Scenario: Presentation cannot carry semantics
  Given the graph_layout / comment / collapsed-state block
  When it is analysed against the evaluator's inputs
  Then it is demonstrated that no field in it reaches evaluation, or the finding is raised as a blocking gap against E35/E37-T01

Scenario: Gaps become tickets
  Given any control gap
  Then it is filed against a specific ticket with an owner and a due sprint, not left as prose in the model

Scenario: Arming cannot be reached from the editor (security edge)
  Then it is verified by inspection and by test that no editor interaction, hotkey or API call path sets rule mode without the SCR-085 step-up flow

Scenario: A Critical/High finding is open at train close (failure)
  Then the epic cannot be Done; the finding is either fixed or carries an Owner-signed accepted-risk record per the R3 security gate
```

Model follows the `04-security-program.md` template with a data-flow diagram in mermaid, trust boundaries annotated, and a threat table. Where a control lives in E35 (server-side compile authority, schema validation, node caps, execution budget), the model records the dependency explicitly rather than duplicating the control.

## Test plan

Missing mappings are filed as gaps. Verification of the tests themselves happens in E37-X02.

This ticket *is* the security work product. Data classification for the editor's data: financial-control configuration — not secret, but integrity-critical, since a silently altered rule can move money on demo today and live after R4.

The DoS branch sets the node/edge caps and the compile request rate limits that E37-S01 and E35 enforce; those numbers are an output of this ticket.

title: Execute abuse cases and the security review of the node editor
body:
## Context
E37-X01 enumerates what could go wrong; this ticket tries it against the running system and closes the loop required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 ("for anything touching keys/withdrawal/RBAC, a manual abuse-case check performed") and the R3 security gate in `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 ("all Critical/High closed; a targeted abuse-case review ... before the train closes"). The rule editor is an order-placing path by proxy, so `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 treats it as `security`-labelled whether or not the label was applied.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execute the abuse cases derived from E37-X01 against staging (demo), each recorded with request/response evidence:
  1. **Crafted save**: submit a rule model containing an action scoped to an account the user cannot trade, and one containing an order-placing action for a manager without live-arming permission → expect 403, no state change, audit row.
  2. **Direct route and API access as viewer** → expect route absent, 403, audit row, no rule content in the response body.
  3. **Semantics smuggled in presentation**: place executable-looking data into `graph_layout`/comment fields → expect it to be ignored by the evaluator and excluded from the hash.
  4. **Hash bypass**: attempt to save a model whose client-claimed hash differs from the server-computed one, and attempt to force-resolve a `Round-trip mismatch` via the API → expect the server to recompute authoritatively and the mismatch to remain blocking and audited.
  5. **Armed-rule mutation**: attempt to modify the active version of an armed rule in place via the API → expect rejection and the new-draft-version path to be the only route.
  6. **Concurrency**: two sessions racing a save → expect optimistic-concurrency rejection, never last-writer-wins.
  7. **Resource abuse**: oversized graph (beyond node/edge caps), deeply nested boolean tree beyond the schema's limits, and a burst of compile requests → expect bounded rejection with a clear error and no backend stall.
  8. **Quarantine**: a corrupted/truncated stored IR → expect read-only, force-disarmed, failing JSON path named, never partially executed.
  9. **Arming bypass**: attempt to set `mode` from the editor context without a step-up token → expect rejection and an audit row.
- SAST/SCA/secrets-scan review of the E37 code and the new editor dependencies (graph + layout libraries), with findings triaged.
- Security review comment on each E37 story and the epic, with any accepted risk explicitly signed off by the Owner.

## Out of scope
- Full pen-test (E43); backend rule-engine sandbox testing (E35); OMS/fan-out abuse cases (E29/E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every abuse case is executed with evidence
  When the review completes
  Then each of the nine cases has a recorded request, response, resulting audit row and a pass/fail verdict

Scenario: Privilege boundaries hold
  Given the crafted-save and viewer-access cases
  Then every attempt returns 403, changes no state, and writes an audit row naming the actor, the attempted action and the denial reason

Scenario: Integrity cannot be talked around (failure path)
  Given the hash-bypass and forced-resolution attempts
  Then the server recomputes the canonical hash itself, the mismatch stays blocking, the resolution choice is audited, and no path exists to persist a rule whose displayed and stored semantics differ

Scenario: Resource abuse is bounded (edge)
  Given an oversized or pathologically nested graph and a burst of compile calls
  Then the server rejects within its caps with a clear error, backend latency stays within budget for other callers, and the editor surfaces the limit rather than hanging

Scenario: A Critical or High finding is open (failure)
  Then E37 cannot be Done until the finding is fixed and re-verified, or an Owner-signed accepted-risk record exists
```

## Technical notes / design
Cases are executed with an API client (not only through the UI) because the UI's own guards are convenience; the server must hold on its own. Test users: owner, manager with `rules:author` and trade permission on one account, manager without live-arming, viewer. Evidence is captured as request/response transcripts plus the corresponding `audit_log` rows, including hash-chain verification for the rows written.

## Test plan
Where a case is automatable it is added to the E2E/contract suites (E37-Q02) so the control cannot regress silently — notably the crafted-save 403, the viewer 403, the concurrency rejection and the cap enforcement. Non-automatable cases are added to the regression pack (E37-Q06).

## Security notes
This is the epic's security verification. Threat classes exercised: elevation of privilege, tampering/integrity, repudiation, denial of service. Data classification: financial-control configuration on demo accounts; no live environment is touched, and no API-key material is involved in any case.

## Accessibility notes
Verifies that the accessible paths (keyboard, node list) enforce the same guards as the pointer paths — an accessible bypass would be a security defect.

## Performance notes
Case 7 measures that abusive input is rejected without degrading other callers, tying into budget #13 (API p95) on the compile/validate endpoints.

## Observability
Confirms every denial and every mismatch resolution produces an audit row in the hash-chained `audit_log`, and that the high-severity integrity-failure telemetry actually alerts.

- [ ] All nine abuse cases executed with evidence and verdicts recorded.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scans clean or findings triaged with dispositions.
- [ ] Automatable controls added to the E2E/contract suites; the rest added to the regression pack.
- [ ] Security engineer review comments posted on E37 and each story; Critical/High closed; any accepted risk Owner-signed.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` and E37-X01's model updated with what execution actually showed.

Blocked by **E37-X01** (the model defines the cases) and **E37-S04** (round-trip and concurrency behaviour must be complete to attack). Feeds the epic's security DoD and E43's pen-test scope.
